result.rationale: The diff shows in GoogleCalendarService deleteEvent: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. In the falsy branch, externalCalendarId is undefined/null, so find can never match and calendarId is always undefined (the previous fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is removed). The same dead predicate appears in updateEvent. Passing an undefined calendarId to calendar.events.delete would fail, so cancellation can succeed in the DB while the calendar event remains — a rea

judged_text: deleteEvent uses the same dead predicate — find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy — so calendarId is undefined whenever the reference's externalCalendarId is missing. Cancelling a booking without a stored externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined and the Google client rejects it, so the event stays on the host's calendar while the booking is cancelled in the database and the cancellation API reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `deleteEvent` (and similarly `updateEvent`) fallback branch is logically dead: `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so it will almost always return `undefined`, leaving `calendarId` unset (or forcing an unintended fallback elsewhere). This matches the finding that deletions can fail or target the wrong calendar when the reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, causing the booking to be cancelled in DB while the external event remains.
